limitations: Unfiltered screen audits retain failures; passing description measurements are not a whole-app accessibility certification.
First largest baseline stopped after four screens; contact lookup/scroll assertions failed and phone setup was not reached. The subsequent unchanged-production baseline reached all six screens.

First candidate search audits failed in test navigation because search hides the navigation bar. Four additional geometry assertions used stale/arbitrary viewport bounds. All original failures are retained.

Final navigation measures current list/navigation/search/tab geometry. The 375x667 physical-Home-button fixture reserves no nonexistent in-app home indicator; the initial two overly conservative geometry failures remain recorded. No audit types or issue handlers were weakened.
VoiceOver service is available only on iOS 27. Its helper temporarily disables VoiceOver for direct page scrolling. Physical gestures and audio acceptance remain unverified.

The six-screen VoiceOver method fails on the complete Phone setup description. A separate native-label probe without ShieldEmptyState or the optional Shield list style also returns only 64 characters despite a complete 68-character accessibility label, before and after waiting two seconds. This narrows the boundary but does not prove the physical announcement or identify the root cause.

The native VoiceOver diagnostic log reports a runner restart after the failed method. Its result bundle records one failed test and no passing tests; the empty restarted suite is not counted as a pass.
The archive is unsigned; device installation, distribution signing, Apple acceptance and real calls remain open.
Independent CI receipt is for base 048272b; it checks the unchanged backend, not Swift.
